title: The ideal cutting out exactly those base changes along which a surjection of modules becomes an isomorphism
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a surjection u : M -> N of A-modules with M projective, an ideal I of A such that for every ring map A -> B the map u tensor 1 is an isomorphism exactly when I is mapped to zero in B (statement lines 6645-6656, tag 05PE). The proof is short but it is a real construction: projectivity is used to replace M by a free module without changing the question, and then the ideal is built from the coefficients of all elements of the kernel with respect to a basis, the equivalence following from the identification of the kernel of the base changed map with the image of the kernel after tensoring. The choice of ideal is the substance, so the claim is H2.
